At a producing pair with positive weights, H_0≥(H_-+H_+)/2>0 and L_0≤(L_-+L_+)/2 give a lower bound by the ratio of sums. That ratio is at least the smaller input weight. Hence the literal weighted target endpoint ceiling suffices on the support graph.

Finite temporary ceilings off the graph bound every producing pair. The finite selection theorem gives convex-order domination with these ceilings. The globally finite convex roof-gap test is nonpositive throughout C and zero under the old law, so the new midpoint law is on the actual graph.

Each interval has one endpoint for each fixed normal. The output within a parity class is bounded by its actual weighted marked atom. At a fixed normal summing at most 2^n classes gives the claimed measure bound, without summing the two normal marks onto one unmarked ceiling.

Conditionally attaching the original mark to the old midpoint and using a martingale kernel to the new midpoint preserves the mark-stratum law and conditional midpoint mean. The subsequent tuple draw preserves the chosen new endpoint marginals.

In the cube calibration there is one compatible base on either side in each parity, and their midpoint is the all-ones base. Exactly 2^n units arrive at its single marked endpoint of reference weight one.
